decisions.reason: As an established core bread variant with visible prior commitment and no reported failure, management would likely continue it rather than reverse a routine extension of the bakery range.
The premium raisin stollen remains a publicly emphasized flagship backed by a gold medal, so reputational commitment and external validation make withdrawal very unlikely.
This rye mixed bread still fits the firm's traditional bread competence and prior launch commitment, though some overlap within the rye assortment leaves a moderate chance of later pruning.

Management would tend to persist with this niche rye variant because it uses existing capabilities and has already been introduced publicly, but its narrower position in a crowded bread line keeps rationalization risk the highest among the breads.
Even as a secondary seasonal stollen beside the flagship, it remains close to the confectionery core and the firm is likely to justify its earlier launch by keeping it for another season.
Having presented this ancient grain bread as a newest Meisterstück, management is likely to stay committed to it because the public framing and artisanal fit make backing away less attractive.
